subject.title: fix: suppress exec-like tool error warnings regardless of includeDetails

question: Should exec-like failures with details be hidden for all includeDetails cases, or should cron, heartbeat, full-verbose, and mutating failure contexts keep visible warnings?
rationale: Current code and tests intentionally surface some exec detail-mode warnings, while the PR asserts blanket suppression; automation cannot choose that user-facing policy safely.

options.title: Clarify And Narrow Policy
options.body: Keep intentional operational/detail warnings unless maintainers explicitly remove them, and revise the fix to cover only the confirmed noisy paths with regression tests.

options.title: Adopt Blanket Suppression
options.body: Accept that all exec-like detail warnings should be hidden, then update the ordering and existing tests to make that new behavior explicit.

options.title: Pause Or Replace Branch
options.body: Leave this PR unmerged or close it in favor of a narrower replacement if the blanket policy is not desired.

recommendation.title: Clarify And Narrow Policy
recommendation.body: Keep intentional operational/detail warnings unless maintainers explicitly remove them, and revise the fix to cover only the confirmed noisy paths with regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work in the mutation and payload warning surfaces makes this the best available routing candidate for the policy choice.
